links.outcome: Reader accuracy, agreement, and reading time with versus without model assistance
links.effect: Accuracy improved for two of three readers (RAD1 76.2% to 83.4%; RAD3 75.6% to 83.4%); Fleiss' kappa 0.432 to 0.642; beneficial decision changes 197 vs detrimental 104 across 1,500 reader-case pairs.
links.quote: Model-assisted reading significantly improved accuracy for two of three readers (RAD1: 76.2 % → 83.4 %, p = 0.001; RAD3: 75.6 % → 83.4 %, p < 0.001; Holm-corrected), with sensitivity gains of 2.4-16.4 percentage points.

links.outcome: Radiologist performance with AI in the reading workflow versus unassisted
links.effect: Assisted reading improved accuracy for two of three readers, cut median interpretation time 33.2% (12.9 to 8.6 s), and raised confidence (all p<0.001).
links.quote: Median interpretation time decreased by 33.2 % overall (12.9 → 8.6 s; p < 0.001), and self-reported confidence increased significantly across all readers (all p < 0.001).

screen.reason: The study conducts a multi-reader multi-case (MRMC) evaluation assessing the impact of AI assistance on radiologist diagnostic performance, reading time, and diagnostic confidence compared to unassisted reading.
